name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER1_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Ascending order of taxonomic categories of mango

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following taxonomic categories of mango (Mangifera indica) in ascending order of the taxonomic hierarchy (from lowest rank to highest rank):

  • Anacardiaceae
  • Dicotyledonae
  • Mangifera
  • Sapindales
  • Angiospermae

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In biological classification, taxonomic categories form a hierarchy of ranks. In ascending order (from lowest to highest rank), the standard sequence of categories for plants is: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Division → Kingdom.

Step 2: Identification of Each Taxon for Mango
For mango (Mangifera indica):
• Mangifera represents the Genus.
• Anacardiaceae represents the Family (note the typical plant family suffix -aceae).
• Sapindales represents the Order (note the typical plant order suffix -ales).
• Dicotyledonae represents the Class.
• Angiospermae represents the Division.

Step 3: Establishing the Ascending Sequence
Placing these taxa from the lowest category (Genus) to the highest category listed (Division) gives:
Mangifera (Genus) → Anacardiaceae (Family) → Sapindales (Order) → Dicotyledonae (Class) → Angiospermae (Division).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct ascending sequence is Mangifera → Anacardiaceae → Sapindales → Dicotyledonae → Angiospermae.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER1_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Descending taxonomic sequence of housefly by common characters

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following taxonomic categories of housefly (Musca domestica) in sequence from the category whose members share the least number of common characteristics to the category whose members share the highest number of common characteristics:

  • Diptera
  • Arthropoda
  • Muscidae
  • Insecta
  • Musca

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
As we move higher in the taxonomic hierarchy from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics shared among members decreases. Conversely, lower the taxon, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share. Therefore, arranging taxa from the least number of common characteristics to the highest number of common characteristics requires a descending order of taxonomic hierarchy (Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus).

Step 2: Identification of Each Taxon for Housefly
For housefly (Musca domestica):
• Arthropoda is the Phylum.
• Insecta is the Class.
• Diptera is the Order.
• Muscidae is the Family (note the animal family suffix -idae).
• Musca is the Genus.

Step 3: Establishing the Descending Sequence
Arranging these categories from the highest rank (Phylum, fewest shared characteristics) down to the lowest rank listed (Genus, most shared characteristics) gives:
Arthropoda (Phylum) → Insecta (Class) → Diptera (Order) → Muscidae (Family) → Musca (Genus).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence from least to highest number of common characteristics is Arthropoda → Insecta → Diptera → Muscidae → Musca.
